title: Biological Classification
syllabus: Five kingdom classification; Salient features and classification of Monera, Protista and Fungi into major groups; Lichens, Viruses, Viroids and Prions

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the main criteria used by R.H. Whittaker (1969) for proposing the Five Kingdom classification system?
options: Presence or absence of cilia and flagella
questions.solution: The main criteria used by R.H. Whittaker for five-kingdom classification were: (1) Cell structure, (2) Body/thallus organisation, (3) Mode of nutrition, (4) Reproduction, and (5) Phylogenetic relationships. Presence or absence of locomotory organelles like cilia/flagella was not a primary criterion.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Archaebacteria and their characteristic habitats:

List-I (Archaebacteria)List-II (Habitat/Feature)
(A) Halophiles(I) Hot sulphur springs
(B) Thermoacidophiles(II) Gut of ruminant animals
(C) Methanogens(III) Extremely saline areas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Halophiles survive in extreme salty areas; Thermoacidophiles thrive in hot, acidic sulphur springs; Methanogens are found in the marshy areas and in the gut of ruminants like cows and buffaloes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding Mycoplasma?
options: They possess a rigid cell wall composed of peptidoglycan.
They are the smallest living cells known.
They can survive completely without oxygen.
Many mycoplasmas are pathogenic in animals and plants.
questions.solution: Mycoplasmas are organisms that completely lack a cell wall. They are the smallest living cells known (approx. 0.3 µm in length), can survive without oxygen, and are pathogenic in many animals and plants.

questions.question: Specialised, thick-walled cells present in cyanobacteria like Nostoc and Anabaena for biological nitrogen fixation are called:
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria such as Nostoc and Anabaena fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized, non-photosynthetic, thick-walled cells called heterocysts, which provide the anaerobic environment needed for the nitrogenase enzyme.

questions.question: Diatomaceous earth is formed due to the indestructible cell wall deposits of diatoms. The cell walls are embedded with:
questions.solution: In diatoms (Chrysophytes), the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells that fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible, leading to the accumulation of diatomaceous earth over billions of years.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the classes of Kingdom Protista and their members:

List-I (Group of Protista)List-II (Example)
(A) Chrysophytes(I) Gonyaulax
(B) Dinoflagellates(II) Diatoms and Desmids
(C) Euglenoids(III) Euglena
(D) Protozoans(IV) Plasmodium

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Chrysophytes include Diatoms and Golden algae (Desmids); Dinoflagellates include red tide-forming Gonyaulax; Euglenoids include Euglena; Sporozoan protozoans include Plasmodium.

questions.question: Red tides in oceans are caused by the rapid multiplication of which of the following organisms?
questions.solution: Red dinoflagellates (e.g., Gonyaulax) undergo such rapid multiplication that they make the sea appear red (red tides) and release toxins (saxitoxin) that can kill marine animals such as fishes.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Euglenoids:
Statement I: Instead of a cell wall, they have a protein-rich layer called pellicle which makes their body flexible.
Statement II: They are photosynthetic in the presence of sunlight, but behave as heterotrophs when deprived of sunlight.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Euglenoids lack a cell wall; instead, they possess a proteinaceous pellicle providing body flexibility. They exhibit mixotrophic nutrition: photosynthetic in sunlight, and heterotrophic (predating on smaller organisms) in the dark.

questions.question: Under suitable conditions, slime moulds form an aggregation called:
questions.solution: Under favourable conditions, slime moulds form an amoeboid aggregation called plasmodium, which may grow and spread over several feet. During unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Protozoan groups and their locomotory structures/examples:

List-I (Group)List-II (Feature / Example)
(A) Amoeboid protozoans(I) Trypanosoma (causes sleeping sickness)
(B) Flagellated protozoans(II) Paramoecium (coordinated ciliary movement)
(C) Ciliated protozoans(III) Entamoeba (moves via pseudopodia)
(D) Sporozoans(IV) Plasmodium (infectious spore-like stage)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Amoeboid: Entamoeba (pseudopodia); Flagellated: Trypanosoma (flagellated parasite); Ciliated: Paramoecium (thousands of coordinated cilia and a gullet); Sporozoans: Plasmodium (malarial parasite with infectious spore stage).

questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is composed of:
questions.solution: The cell walls of true fungi are composed of chitin (a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine) and complex polysaccharides.

questions.question: A continuous fungal mycelium filled with multinucleated cytoplasm without cross-walls (septa) is described as:
questions.solution: When hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm and lack cross-walls (septa), they are termed aseptate and coenocytic (characteristic of Phycomycetes).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the classes of Kingdom Fungi and their common names:

List-I (Class)List-II (Common Name)
(A) Phycomycetes(I) Club fungi
(B) Ascomycetes(II) Imperfect fungi
(C) Basidiomycetes(III) Algal fungi
(D) Deuteromycetes(IV) Sac fungi

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Phycomycetes: Algal fungi; Ascomycetes: Sac fungi; Basidiomycetes: Club fungi; Deuteromycetes: Imperfect fungi (lacking sexual stages).

questions.question: Which of the following members belongs to Phycomycetes and is a parasitic fungus on mustard?
questions.solution: Albugo candida is an obligate parasitic fungus on mustard leaves causing white rust disease and belongs to the class Phycomycetes.

questions.question: Which of the following Ascomycetes is extensively used in biochemical and genetic research?
questions.solution: Neurospora crassa (pink bread mould) is used extensively in biochemical and genetic research (often termed the 'Drosophila of the plant kingdom').

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the reproduction in Ascomycetes:
Statement I: Asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores.
Statement II: Sexual spores are ascospores produced endogenously in sac-like asci.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: In Ascomycetes, asexual conidia are formed exogenously on conidiophores, while sexual ascospores are formed endogenously inside sac-like asci which are arranged in ascocarps.

questions.question: Dikaryon stage ($n + n$, i.e., two nuclei per cell) is a prominent intermediate phase during the sexual cycle of:
questions.solution: In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, plasmogamy is not immediately followed by karyogamy; an intervening dikaryotic stage ($n + n$) occurs where cells possess two nuclei.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding Basidiomycetes and their common representative forms:

List-I (Genus)List-II (Common Name / Disease)
(A) Agaricus(I) Rust fungus
(B) Ustilago(II) Mushroom
(C) Puccinia(III) Smut fungus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Agaricus is the common edible mushroom; Ustilago causes smut disease; Puccinia causes wheat rust disease.

questions.question: Why are Deuteromycetes commonly known as 'Fungi Imperfecti'?
options: Only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.
They do not have a true nucleus.
They do not possess any cell wall.
questions.solution: Deuteromycetes are called imperfect fungi because only their asexual (conidial) or vegetative stages are known. When sexual (perfect) stages are discovered, they are moved to Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of fungi belongs EXCLUSIVELY to Deuteromycetes?
questions.solution: Alternaria, Colletotrichum, and Trichoderma are classic examples of Deuteromycetes.

questions.question: Viruses are not included in Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification because:
options: They are non-cellular entities and do not possess truly living cellular organisation
They reproduce only by binary fission
questions.solution: Viruses are non-cellular, inert crystalline structures outside living host cells, and thus do not possess true cellular organization to be classified in Whittaker's cellular five-kingdom system.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the scientific milestones in the discovery of viruses:

List-I (Scientist)List-II (Discovery / Concept)
(A) Dmitri Ivanowsky (1892)(I) Crystallised viruses and showed they consist largely of proteins
(B) M.W. Beijerinek (1898)(II) Recognised microbes smaller than bacteria causing Tobacco Mosaic Disease
(C) W.M. Stanley (1935)(III) Coined the phrase Contagium vivum fluidum (infectious living fluid)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Ivanowsky (1892) discovered that the causal agent of tobacco mosaic disease passed through bacteria-proof filters; Beijerinck (1898) called the filtered extract Contagium vivum fluidum; Stanley (1935) first demonstrated that viruses can be crystallized into protein crystals.

questions.question: Bacteriophages (viruses that infect bacteria) usually possess:
questions.solution: Bacterial viruses or bacteriophages usually have double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) as their genetic material. Plant viruses typically contain ssRNA, while animal viruses may contain ssRNA, dsRNA, or dsDNA.

questions.question: The protein coat of a virus is called capsid, which is composed of small subunits called:
questions.solution: The protein shell that encloses the viral nucleic acid is the capsid, made up of repeating small protein subunits called capsomeres arranged in helical or polyhedral geometric forms.

questions.question: Viroids differ from viruses in that viroids have:
options: Free RNA of low molecular weight without a protein coat
DNA molecule enclosed by a protein coat
RNA molecule enclosed by a protein coat
Free DNA molecule without a protein coat
questions.solution: Discovered by T.O. Diener (1971), viroids are infectious agents smaller than viruses that cause Potato Spindle Tuber Disease. They consist solely of a short strand of free circular ssRNA of low molecular weight and lack a protein capsid.

questions.question: Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) or Mad Cow Disease in cattle and its human analogue Cr-Jacob disease (CJD) are caused by:
questions.solution: Prions are neurological infectious agents consisting exclusively of abnormally folded protein particles. They cause Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) in cattle and Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) in humans.

questions.question: In Lichens, the algal component is called ________ and the fungal component is called ________:
questions.solution: In a lichen, the autotrophic algal partner is called the phycobiont (prepares food) and the heterotrophic fungal partner is called the mycobiont (provides shelter and absorbs minerals/water).

questions.question: Lichens are known to be very sensitive pollution indicators, particularly for:
questions.solution: Lichens are sensitive bio-indicators of atmospheric air pollution, especially $\text{SO}_2$; they do not grow in polluted industrial areas and cities.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Archaebacteria differ from other bacteria in having a different cell wall structure.
Statement II: This unique cell wall structure is responsible for their survival under extreme environmental conditions.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Archaebacteria possess a distinctive branched-lipid monolayer/pseudomurein cell wall structure that lacks peptidoglycan, enabling them to survive in extreme habitats like high salinity, high acidity, and boiling temperatures.

questions.question: Citrus canker is a plant disease caused by:
questions.solution: Citrus canker is a widespread bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri.

questions.question: Heterotrophic bacteria are most abundant in nature. Which of the following is NOT an important beneficial role of heterotrophic bacteria?
options: Fixing carbon dioxide into carbohydrates through anoxygenic photosynthesis
Fixing nitrogen in roots of legume plants (Rhizobium)
questions.solution: Fixing $\text{CO}_2$ into carbohydrates via photosynthesis is performed by autotrophic bacteria (chemoautotrophs or photoautotrophs), not heterotrophic bacteria.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the shapes of bacteria:

List-I (Morphological Type)List-II (Shape)
(A) Coccus(I) Rod-shaped
(B) Bacillus(II) Comma-shaped
(C) Spirillum(III) Spherical
(D) Vibrio(IV) Spiral

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Coccus: Spherical; Bacillus: Rod-shaped; Spirillum: Spiral-shaped; Vibrio: Comma-shaped.

questions.question: Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria obtain energy for ATP synthesis by oxidizing:
options: Inorganic substances like nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia
questions.solution: Chemosynthetic autotrophs (such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter) oxidize various inorganic substances such as nitrates, nitrites, and ammonia and use the released energy for ATP production, playing a role in recycling nutrients like N, P, Fe, and S.

questions.question: Which kingdom in Whittaker's system forms a biological link with plants, animals, and fungi?
questions.solution: Kingdom Protista includes all unicellular eukaryotic organisms and forms an evolutionary link with the other multicellular eukaryotic kingdoms (Plantae, Animalia, and Fungi).

questions.question: Resting spores of slime moulds possess:
options: True cellulose cell walls and are extremely resistant
Siliceous walls with two overlapping valves
questions.solution: The spores of slime moulds possess true, rigid cell walls composed of cellulose. They are resistant to adverse conditions and survive for many years, dispersed by air currents.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the fungal structures and their reproductive nature:

List-I (Spore/Body)List-II (Nature of Formation)
(A) Conidia(I) Endogenous sexual spores
(B) Ascospores(II) Exogenous asexual spores
(C) Basidiospores(III) Endogenous asexual spores
(D) Sporangiospores(IV) Exogenous sexual spores

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Conidia: Exogenous asexual spores (Ascomycetes); Ascospores: Endogenous sexual spores (Ascomycetes); Basidiospores: Exogenous sexual spores produced on basidium (Basidiomycetes); Sporangiospores/Zoospores: Endogenous asexual spores (Phycomycetes).

questions.question: Morels (Morchella) and truffles are delicacies belonging to which class of fungi?
questions.solution: Morels and truffles are edible members belonging to the class Ascomycetes.

questions.question: Which of the following fungal associations represents a mutualistic relationship between a fungus and the roots of higher plants?
questions.solution: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between a fungus (e.g., Glomus) and the roots of higher plants (e.g., Pinus), where the fungus aids in phosphorus and nutrient uptake while receiving sugars from the plant.

questions.question: Sex organs are absent, but plasmogamy is brought about by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains/genotypes in:
questions.solution: In Basidiomycetes, differentiated sex organs are absent. Plasmogamy occurs by somatogamy (fusion of two somatic or vegetative cells of different strains), giving rise to a dikaryotic mycelium that forms basidia.

questions.question: Puccinia causes which of the following agricultural plant diseases?
questions.solution: Puccinia graminis tritici is a heteroecious basidiomycete fungus that causes black rust (wheat rust) of wheat crops.

questions.question: Karyogamy and meiosis take place inside the basidium to produce how many basidiospores?
questions.solution: Inside the basidium, karyogamy and meiosis produce 4 haploid basidiospores born exogenously on sterigmata.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding Cyanobacteria:
Statement I: Cyanobacteria possess chlorophyll a similar to green plants and are photosynthetic autotrophs.
Statement II: They often form blooms in polluted water bodies and are surrounded by a gelatinous sheath.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are oxygenic photosynthetic prokaryotes with chlorophyll a. They are unicellular, colonial, or filamentous, surrounded by a mucilaginous sheath, and often form blooms in eutrophic waters.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT caused by a virus in humans?
questions.solution: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. Mumps (Paramyxovirus), Smallpox (Variola virus), and AIDS (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) are all viral diseases.

questions.question: Diatoms are the chief 'producers' in the oceans. They float passively in water currents as:
questions.solution: Diatoms are microscopic unicellular algae that float passively in water currents (plankton) and serve as primary producers in marine ecosystems.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the kingdom and cell wall composition in Whittaker's Five Kingdom Classification:

List-I (Kingdom)List-II (Cell Wall Composition)
(A) Monera(I) Non-cellulosic (Chitin and polysaccharides)
(B) Protista(II) Cellulosic cell wall present in all members
(C) Fungi(III) Non-cellulosic (Polysaccharide + amino acid / peptidoglycan)
(D) Plantae(IV) Present in some (e.g., diatoms, dinoflagellates), absent in others

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Monera: Non-cellulosic peptidoglycan; Protista: Present in some (chrysophytes, dinoflagellates), absent in others (protozoans, euglenoids); Fungi: Chitin and polysaccharides; Plantae: True cellulosic cell wall.
